r3FindingResolution.reason: Nonempty slotReasons rows carry typed priming, warmup and measured identities. Warmup-only record failure is representable without corrupting measured positions, and coverage consults the correct slot. All seven measured-series positions and valid aggregates can be retained.

QD-27 maps reasons to affected quantities, separates evidence failure from measurement availability, preserves all four numeric samples for missing/invalid operational records, and independently preserves aggregates when their inputs exist. Any affected slot still makes the batch incomplete and non-Q6. Schema and declared semantic checks agree for the listed cases.

requiredFindings.title: Join host kernel-start identities through an explicit bridge, not a later notification interval
requiredFindings.relation: New error introduced in the response to C2-Q0-R3-N01
requiredFindings.problem: The new host join requires the host's process start to lie in the interval from the fork-event timestamp to the terminal record. The stated process identity uses kernel start time, which is assigned before the fork connector is invoked; the connector timestamps its later notification. A genuine process start therefore precedes the proposed interval's lower endpoint. The raw fields also use different clock representations: /proc stat22 is boot-time ticks, while connector timestamps use monotonic nanoseconds.

counterexample.assumptions: Single TGID lifetime on an unsuspended host, with units and clock domains normalized; no event loss or reuse ambiguity.
counterexample.result: The host start is outside [100.001,100.200], so the stated rule returns no match and forces unjoinable-identity/incomplete despite a correct host record.

requiredFindings.impact: Otherwise valid host RSS observations are systematically rejected under the stated kernel-start identity. Conservative incomplete status prevents false PASS, but breaks the intended complete-run path.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Retain an explicit same-generation bridge between the host kernel-start identity and the harness lifetime generation, defining clock domains, units and tick quantization. Join through that bridge, or specify a sound generation-bound method whose lower endpoint can precede actual creation. Keep unavailable or ambiguous bridges incomplete. Add a design reference case in which a valid kernel start precedes its fork notification and joins correctly; do not discard an unmatched host value.

sources.evidence: start_time/start_boottime are assigned at lines 2181-2182 before proc_fork_connector at 2279.
proc_fork_connector timestamps the notification using ktime_get_ns at line 120.
stat22 derives from timens-adjusted start_boottime converted to clock ticks at lines 552-554.
